blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine government is weighing a shorter maturity for its planned retail dollar bond (RDB) sale later this year, seeking to keep borrowing costs in check as elevated interest rates threaten to make longer-dated debt more expensive. In an interview, National Treasurer Sharon Almanza told that reporters the offering would begin after the government completes its ongoing retail treasury bond (RTB) sale. She said investors could demand higher yields if the dollar bonds carry longer maturities.
